Q: Are ADATA SSD compatible with different operating systems? 

ADATA SSDs are designed in accordance with the Serial ATA International Organization standards and have undergone rigorous testing to ensure they work with various operating systems.

1. NVMe (PCIe) M.2 SSDs require Windows 8.1 or later to support the NVMe driver (we recommend Windows 10 for better the best experience and usability). Linux, including Fedora, SUSE, Ubuntu, and Red Hat, is also supported.

2. AHCI(SATA) M.2 SSDs can be used with Windows 7 or later.

 Q: Do I need to defragment my SSD? 

Since SSDs don't have mechanical drives, so there is no need for defragmentation. Defragmenting an SSD may cause unnecessary wear and tear. SSDs are designed to write data evenly on the entire drive as much as possible, thereby reducing excessive wear on any one location.

 Q: Do I need to install a driver to use my SSD? 

ADATA SSDs can use standard drivers, which can be applied to different operating systems; at the same time, users can also install the drivers officially provided by the motherboard manufacturers. If you have other questions, please contact ADATA's customer service center.

1. NVMe (PCIe) M.2 SSDs require Windows 8.1 or later to support the NVMe driver (it is recommended to update to Windows 10 or later). Linux series such as Fedora, SUSE, Ubuntu, Red Hat are also supported

2. AHCI (SATA) M.2 SSDs are compatible with Windows 7 and later

 Q: How do I setup RAID 0? 

Set up RAID 0 on a compatible motherboard, then connect two SSDs of the same specification to the set port. For detailed instructions, please refer to your motherboard's user manual. The performance of the SSD with a RAID 0 configuration will be double that of a single SSD.

...

Q: Why is my existing SATA SSD not being recognized after installing a new SATA / NVMe M.2 SSDs? 

If you encounter this problem, please refer to your motherboard's user manual or the manufacturer's website. Motherboards vary by model and brand. The type and quantity of I/O ports are not the same; therefore, when a SATA or NVMe M.2 SSD is inserted into the slot, it may be affected by I/O. The sharing of channels by the ports results in a limited number of channels supported by the chipset, rendering some 7pin SATA sockets unusable.

 Q: If my computer only supports PCIe Gen3, can it still work with a PCIe Gen5 SSD? 

PCs that do not support PCIe Gen5 SSDs can still use the said SSDs. However, the SSDs performance will be limited to PCIe Gen3 levels. 

 Q: How do I know if my PC can support PCIe Gen5 SSDs? 

Firstly check the make and specifications of your motherboard on the manufacturers website to see if it has M.2 slots that support PCIe 5x4. If there are two M.2 PCIe 5x4 slots, you can use the direct link to the CPU terminal (center Processor) M.2 socket for better performance.

 Q: How do I install my new SSD onto my motherboard? 

Firstly, confirmed your SSDs form factor - M.2, mSATA, or SATA. Locate the correct slot type on your motherboard, insert your SSD and secure it with screws. For video instructions, M.2 SSD on desktop please click here, M.2 SSD on laptop please click here.

#### Coolest Games Time - Next-Level Gen5 Gear

The MARS 980 PRO is a gaming PCIe 5.0 SSD with air cooling for quiet, stable performance. Featuring PCIe Gen5 x4 and NVMe 2.0 support, it excels in AI workloads and supports the latest Intel and AMD platforms—built to break boundaries.

#### Boss Mode On. Enemies Down.

The MARS 980 PRO features a sequential read/write speed of 14,000/13,000MB per second, which is double the performance of PCIe Gen4 SSDs and 8x faster than standard Gen3 SSDs. It is fully backward compatible with PCIe 4.0 and 3.0 platforms. Complete every challenge in mere seconds!

Not only does the MARS 980 PRO fit perfectly into the PS5'a drive slot, it also provides a smooth and no-lag gaming experience while enjoying triple A masterpieces.

...

Carefully selected 232-layer 3D NAND flash memory allows the MARS 980 PRO to feature an ultra-large capacity of up to 8TB, and the SSD uses a variety of data protection and error correction technologies to greatly improve TBW (Total Bytes Written) and durability to meet high load requirements.

...

#### The Gaming Gen5 SSD for Laptops

It’s finally here! MARS 980 BLADE is a gaming Gen5 SSD built for laptops, featuring PCIe Gen5 x4 and NVMe 2.0 support. Its compact design ensures stable performance even in tight spaces, optimized for AI workloads and compatible with the latest Intel and AMD platforms. No matter where it's installed, it's built to go beyond the limits.

#### Clutch Moment. Legendary Move.

The MARS 980 BLADE features a sequential read/write speed of 14,000/13,000MB per second, which is double the performance of PCIe Gen4 SSDs and 8x faster than standard Gen3 SSDs. It is fully backward compatible with PCIe 4.0 and 3.0 platforms. Complete every challenge in mere seconds!

#### 6nm Control, Game Changer

Built with TSMC’s advanced 6nm process, the MARS 980 BLADE delivers superior performance-to-power efficiency, reducing heat generation in PCIe 5.0 SSDs and eliminating the need for bulky cooling—making it ideal for laptops and compact systems.

...

Carefully selected 232-layer 3D NAND flash memory allows the MARS 980 BLADE to feature an ultra-large capacity of up to 8TB, and the SSD uses a variety of data protection and error correction technologies to greatly improve TBW (Total Bytes Written) and durability to meet high load requirements.
